2.2B total frozen of USDT and USDC!

The Binance hot wallet 0x28c6…1d60 was made to carry an EIP-7702 delegation (code 0xef0100 + 63e842b0…) pointing at a wallet-drainer implementation — the same kit flagged pre-drain for operator 0x7c8601d4 (Tornado-funded). In this tx the operator EOA (NOT the account owner) called sweep(address recipient, address[] tokens) = selector 0x8a179be4, and the delegate code transferred the wallet’s entire token inventory — ~1.62B USDT, 167K ETH, UNI, LINK, PEPE, ENA, wBETH, xaut, PAXG, WBTC and ~60 other assets — to attacker collection address 0x5227f603c1ee34ce3c06efe6477003bdfccb2f8c. Net ~$2.53B drained. Setting a 7702 delegation requires a signature from the account’s own key, so this is a signing/private-key compromise of an exchange hot wallet, extracted via an operator-gated universal sweep.

posts.name: Justin Kalland
posts.text:
A potential slip by the Binance attacker? @MetaMask should preserve whatever web2 logs they can.

The attacker sent 175M USDT to a fresh wallet.

About 2.5 minutes later, that wallet also received 2 ETH. Likely for gas, matching the pattern used with their other attack wallets.

Exactly two minutes after that, it used MetaMask's Gas Station. Despite already having gas.

Three consecutive transactions landed in the same block: an ETH top-up from Gas Station, an unlimited USDT approval for @KyberNetwork's router, and a payment of 127.67 USDT to Gas Station.

The ETH top up exactly matched the combined maximum gas budgets of the Kyber approval and the USDT payment. Down to the wei.

But they already had more than enough ETH to cover both.

My theory: they were using MetaMask Wallet and, while rushing, selected USDT for gas by mistake 

MetaMask sometimes defaults like this for convenience. And the same block top-up sequence matches how their implementation works.

To use Gas Station in MetaMask you have to use MetaMask Sentinel. Meaning the transactions go through them, not a regular RPC.

That interaction probablly left offchain records with MetaMask, potentially including IP metadata.

Among all the attacker wallets I checked, this was the only one showing Gas Station usage.

The wallet: 0xAa246BF639586a6Ba46762D378CE50cA4fc654a0

Binance Hack: $6.01B Stolen, $2.80B Frozen

The Binance Hacker took $6.01B from Binance hot wallets on nine chains between 20:10 and 23:05 UTC on 29 October. 

Issuers have frozen $2.80B of it. $2.9B in ETH, BTC, TRX, SOL and altcoins is still movable.

ZachXBT: Stolen Funds from the $6.3B Binance Exploit and $388M Bitget Exploit Commingled at Same Address, Suspected Same Attacker

ZachXBT posted that stolen funds from the $6.3 billion Binance exploit and the $388 million Bitget exploit arrived via THORChain and were commingled at the same address. ZachXBT stated that this indicates the same actor is likely behind both incidents. The Bitget exploit had previously been attributed to the North Korea-linked TraiderTraitor, which has overlap with other previous exploits such as Kelp DAO.

According to MistTrack, stolen TRX from the Binance incident flowed through Bitget Wallet Swap Bridge into an address beginning with 0xCd68. On-chain tracking shows that this address was previously used by the Phemex hacker.
